title: Optimizing LLMs in Insurance with DSPy: Jeronim Morina
talk_summary: An insurance data lab describes moving from hand-tuned prompts to DSPy-style program optimization, but the real content is the prerequisite discipline: define the problem with domain experts, instrument traces, build labeled eval sets, and write custom metrics before optimizing anything. They explicitly warn DSPy has a steep learning curve and is not a guaranteed win.

takeaways.what_they_do: They scraped production data into clean input/output pairs with labels before touching any optimizer, and warn about data leakage where the label is deducible from the input.
takeaways.evidence_quote: please don't stumble upon this data leakage is still a thing

takeaways.technique: Start with cheap deterministic metrics, add LLM-judge only later
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend beginning with regex/string-comparison evals and only then layering LLM judges, rather than jumping to fuzzy 'looks good' judgments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start with some small evaluations like regx or string comparisons and then only then use techniques like LMS judge

takeaways.technique: Trace inspection of what tools actually send
takeaways.what_they_do: They used mitmproxy and Arize Phoenix tracing to see the real prompts and call graph behind chaining libraries, because hardcoded templates were opaque.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use mitm proxy and to really inspect like what are all these tools used

takeaways.technique: Decompose into modules, not one giant prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: They split the task into separate modules (retriever, multihop QA, final answer) so each step can be evaluated and tuned in isolation, warning against one huge ReAct prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't come up with one huge uh react when we did this and is bad

takeaways.technique: Prompt sensitivity as a red flag
takeaways.what_they_do: They observed small prompt edits caused large output swings, and patching with more error-handling code produced a fragile system they refused to ship.
takeaways.evidence_quote: very small prom changes led to very high problems in the end

takeaways.what_they_do: Despite the title, the speaker says DSPy's learning curve is steep and it is 'not a 100% recommendation', and that it fails without clean data and metrics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the learning curve is quite Steep and it's maybe a bit too much overall
